one_line: Agent-assisted shopping and purchase planning for a Nigerian marketplace.
what_it_does: Exposes structured tools to search products, discover stores, compare options, and prepare a human-reviewed purchase plan, with a manual fallback.
leverage_rationale: Typed marketplace and planning tools improve precision and repeatability, but a general agent could perform much of this through the visible marketplace UI with friction.
leverage_evidence: Four read-only tools are described: search_products, discover_stores, compare_products, prepare_purchase_plan.
Tools return structured prices, stock, seller details, and review links.
Purchase and payment remain human-controlled.
execution_rationale: The live demo is reported alive and the packet describes a coherent MVP, but the pitch is extremely thin and no video or reliable end-to-end visual proof is available.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive and gallery_images=2.
Description states manual and WebMCP paths share marketplace logic.
No video and frame evidence is blurry/repetitive.
impact_rationale: There is a concrete audience of shoppers navigating a real Nigerian marketplace and a credible convenience and safety benefit.
impact_evidence: Real public marketplace data is claimed.
Product comparison and local-store discovery address shopping friction.
Human review boundary reduces purchase risk.
creativity_rationale: A sensible agent-shopping synthesis with a human approval boundary, but not a highly novel interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Structured shopping and purchase-plan workflow.
Explicitly omits checkout/payment tools.
usability_note: Likely useful for discovery and comparison; thin product evidence limits confidence in polish.
red_flags: Very generic pitch and sparse submission evidence.
No video despite referenced frame sheets.
standouts: Human-in-the-loop purchase planning is appropriately bounded.
advance_reason: Credible concept but insufficient evidence and modest WebMCP delta.

one_line: An SDK that observes website use and generates approved WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Records network activity and user workflows, uses an agent to propose tool definitions, tests them in a sandbox, and exports approved JavaScript tools.
leverage_rationale: The product directly addresses the cost of creating page-owned tools and supports dynamic tool registration; general UI-driving agents cannot replicate this authoring workflow comparably well.
leverage_evidence: One-script SDK observes existing site behavior and network requests.
Agent forges tools, sandbox-tests them, seeks approval, and exports code.
Demo transcript describes tools becoming available immediately after forging.
execution_rationale: The 220-second video transcript and frame sheet show a coherent authoring-to-use flow with an ecommerce demo, though some implementation claims remain unobserved.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive, public repo present, video duration 220 seconds.
Transcript covers toolkit install, search/add-to-cart/order, forging, approval, and exported tools.
Frames visibly show ToolForge and the ceramics-shop interface.
impact_rationale: It targets a real bottleneck for product teams: turning existing web apps into reliable agent surfaces without hand-authoring every schema.
impact_evidence: Drop-in script and export-to-repository workflow are concrete adoption path.
Existing website behavior is reused rather than requiring a new agent-native app.
creativity_rationale: The observe, infer, sandbox, approve, and export interaction model is an original and memorable application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Tool generation from observed real usage/network behavior.
Dynamic forge_tool registration during an active session.
Human approval gates generated tools.
usability_note: The guided inspect-and-approve workflow appears understandable and practical for developers.
red_flags: Generated tool correctness and security depend on agent inference and sandbox coverage.
standouts: Strong end-to-end video evidence and unusually direct WebMCP leverage.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP-native developer workflow with strong demonstrated execution.

one_line: An agent translates natural print requests into a reviewed local print-shop order.
what_it_does: Reads print context, proposes cost/readability/speed plans, compares nearby shops, applies settings, and opens checkout while leaving payment to the human.
leverage_rationale: Printing involves many precise coupled settings and real-world consequences; structured context and plan tools are materially safer and more reliable than UI guessing.
leverage_evidence: Nine typed tools cover context, upload, planning, comparison, preparation, status, and checkout review.
Plans expose sheet count, price, tradeoffs, capability, and ETA.
No place_order/pay_order tools; human retains confirmation and payment.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and thoughtfully bounded, but there is no video and only limited visual evidence of the central workflow.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive and gallery_images=2.
Detailed description specifies end-to-end planning and checkout-review behavior.
No video evidence and frame sheets are indirect.
impact_rationale: It addresses a specific, common usability problem for people who need printing but do not understand print-shop settings, with clear real-world value.
impact_evidence: Natural-language goals such as cheap, readable, ready tonight are translated into actionable plans.
Nearby real shops, prices, capabilities, and ETA are compared.
Human payment boundary fits consequential physical orders.
creativity_rationale: The combination of document-aware print planning, tradeoff explanations, and a deliberately human-controlled checkout is a fresh, deeply pursued interaction.
creativity_evidence: Four explicit plan objectives including readability and eco tradeoffs.
Agent changes the page's live draft but cannot pay.
usability_note: The goal-oriented plans and visible draft changes should reduce expert print terminology burden.
red_flags: No video or public repository; central live behavior is claimed rather than demonstrated.
standouts: Excellent safety boundary for a real-world transaction.
advance_reason: High-impact, strongly WebMCP-shaped workflow despite incomplete visual proof.

one_line: A tabletop narrative game where the agent plays a constrained companion.
what_it_does: Registers and unregisters typed speech and action tools according to a character's skills, state, and world context so the agent cannot perform unavailable behaviors.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the game mechanic: the live registry enforces character capability boundaries that prompting alone cannot reliably enforce.
leverage_evidence: Typed speech acts replace unrestricted free-text speech.
Tools register/unregister as character and room state changes.
The UI reads the live registry and shows unavailable actions struck out.
execution_rationale: The packet gives unusually specific mechanics and the visual frames show a coherent art-directed game/interface, though no video limits direct proof of play completion.
execution_evidence: Detailed character constraints include warmth, nerve, skills, and room transitions.
Frames show Party of Two title, character cards, and narrative UI states.
demo_alive=alive and gallery_images=1.
impact_rationale: It serves solo tabletop and interactive-fiction players with a clear unmet desire for an actual second player rather than a narrator.
impact_evidence: Explicit target of solo tabletop players.
Agent opposition and refusal are core to the play experience.
creativity_rationale: This is a genuinely novel interaction model that turns agent tool availability into diegetic character agency and game rules.
creativity_evidence: Character abilities are functions that literally do not exist when disallowed.
No free-text speech escape hatch.
Live registry is presented as the authoritative game state.
usability_note: The constrained tool surface should make the agent's role legible, though the narrative interface may require learning.
red_flags: No video means actual agent play and state transitions are not directly verified.
standouts: Strong conceptual integrity: rules are enforced by capability existence, not prompts.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP use and standout originality for an agent-native game.

one_line: A synthetic Colombian telecom registry with an agent twin for every validated action.
what_it_does: Lets users upload documents, extract and review dossier fields, submit and modify records, and manage status manually or through page-owned agent tools.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools share the same validation and authority as buttons, preventing an agent from skipping procedural steps or bypassing the page's logic.
leverage_evidence: Every button has an AI-agent twin using the same validation.
Agent is blocked from skipping dossier steps.
Review fields cite exact source document and page before human approval.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a broad, coherent workflow with multilingual UI, document provenance, edits, cancellation, submission, and listing, supported by a live demo and repository.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive, public repo present, gallery_images=6.
Frames show Nexo RUTIC workflow and manual/agent path messaging.
Description covers upload through approval, modification, cancellation, and status checks.
impact_rationale: Government procedures are high-friction and error-sensitive; a validated, source-cited assistant can provide substantial value to applicants and administrators.
impact_evidence: Concrete telecom-provider registry procedure.
Local extraction keeps PDFs away from the model.
Spanish/English support and document/page citations improve accessibility and trust.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to a bounded government trámite with paired manual and sentence paths is a fresh, well-developed concept.
creativity_evidence: Every action explicitly names button and agent sentence.
Human-approved submission code and immutable last-submitted version handling.
usability_note: Step gating, bilingual UI, and provenance review support a demanding workflow.
red_flags: Synthetic government app; real-world deployment constraints are not demonstrated.
standouts: Strong shared validation and provenance model for consequential forms.
advance_reason: High-quality, consequential workflow with strong WebMCP leverage and evidence.

one_line: A collaborative map where agents help groups negotiate places and private constraints.
what_it_does: Combines shared and private needs, live venue elimination, agent research, and private opt-out suggestions in a synchronized planning room.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables each person's agent to advocate within a shared live room while preserving agent-only knowledge; general UI driving cannot comparably preserve this authority and privacy model.
leverage_evidence: Three people share a live map and brief.
Needs can be shared, private, or agent-only; agent-only needs never reach the server.
Agent can research hollow venue data and propose places to the group.
execution_rationale: The 174-second explainer provides a clear, coherent end-to-end story of room creation, invite, constraints, privacy, negotiation, and research, with live demo and frames.
execution_evidence: Video transcript demonstrates setup, invite code, synchronized map, private constraints, opt-out, and agent research.
Frames show map UI, participant markers, venue labels, and mobile/desktop states.
demo_alive=alive.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real recurring group-coordination problem while protecting sensitive preferences and making tradeoffs visible without forcing disclosure.
impact_evidence: Dietary, budget, timing, and undisclosed vetoes are explicit use cases.
Private constraints affect results without exposing their reason or owner.
Agent research fills missing venue information for everyone.
creativity_rationale: The privacy-preserving multi-agent negotiation model is original, memorable, and pursued beyond a basic group poll.
creativity_evidence: Agent-only needs remain local while their effects can still shape advocacy.
Private opt-out paths quantify what becomes possible if a constraint is relaxed.
Map remains honest about unknown venue data.
usability_note: Single composer, invite link, visible effects, and private escape hatches make complex coordination legible.
red_flags: Privacy and trust claims would need deeper observation in Stage 2.
standouts: Excellent integration of live shared state, personal agents, and privacy.
advance_reason: A compelling, well-demonstrated use of WebMCP for shared coordination with private agency.

one_line: A deterministic mobility scenario lab for agents and human researchers.
what_it_does: Lets agents build, perturb, compare, and analyze synthetic mobility scenarios so humans can inspect reproducible evidence before real-world pilots.
leverage_rationale: Structured scenario construction and deterministic comparison are much more reliable than an agent clicking a complex simulation dashboard, though the underlying simulation concept could exist behind other APIs.
leverage_evidence: Agent builds and breaks synthetic scenarios.
Product emphasizes same assumptions, constraints, demand, and disruptions for comparisons.
Human uses deterministic evidence as source of truth rather than agent prose.
execution_rationale: The concept and v0.5 framing are coherent, and the live demo/repository support a real prototype, but no video or detailed end-to-end visual evidence is provided.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive, public repo present, gallery_images=4.
Frames show NEO/LAB branding and dark mobility visualization/dashboard states.
Description identifies scenario comparison and analysis workflow.
impact_rationale: Mobility planners and researchers have expensive, consequential pilot decisions and need reproducible early evidence; this directly targets that need.
impact_evidence: Explicit audiences include planners, researchers, and R&D teams.
Addresses setup-code and specialist-toolchain friction.
Deterministic scenario evidence supports comparing alternatives before pilots.
creativity_rationale: The agent-as-experiment-operator framing and resilient scenario testing are a strong synthesis for mobility research.
creativity_evidence: Build it, break it, make it resilient workflow.
Combines agent ideation with deterministic evidence rather than generated conclusions.
usability_note: Could lower specialist-tool friction, but the dashboard and research workflow may still be complex.
red_flags: v0.5 and absent video leave core simulation behavior under-evidenced.
standouts: Clear epistemic boundary between agent operation and deterministic evidence.
advance_reason: High impact and meaningful WebMCP leverage; needs Stage 2 observation for execution confirmation.

one_line: A game where an AI agent plays through the site while humans observe agent-specific semantics.
what_it_does: Separates human-like and agent-like actions in a social matching/game environment and exposes state and tool access for an agent visitor.
leverage_rationale: Semantic action identity and agent-readable state add meaningful structure, but the described game could largely be driven by a general agent with enough UI context.
leverage_evidence: send_human_like and send_agent_like distinguish action meaning.
Submission emphasizes communicating who acts, current state, and what happens next.
Frames show Meet the Queen, tool-access panel, and agent/human captions.
execution_rationale: The visual packet shows a coherent branded game/demo interface and the live repository is present, but the core game loop and agent invocation are not directly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive and public repo present.
Frames show repeated Meet the Queen UI states and tool-access area.
No video and limited readable detail.
impact_rationale: It offers a plausible experimental audience interested in agent-native games and semantics, but the practical value beyond a conceptual demonstration is less established.
impact_evidence: Clear target is future-facing agent/game interaction.
Humans watch an agent play a site.
creativity_rationale: Treating agent actions as semantically distinct from human actions is an interesting conceptual direction, even if the game surface is lightly evidenced.
creativity_evidence: Agent-specific action meaning rather than disguised human clicks.
Site and agent are framed as participants in an environment.
usability_note: Observation-oriented interface is legible, but the packet does not show enough playable flow.
red_flags: No video; core claims are conceptual and small UI text is unreadable.
standouts: Explicit semantic distinction between human and agent actions.
advance_reason: Interesting concept, but insufficient demonstrated product depth relative to stronger entries.

one_line: A shared Unicode canvas where agents edit structured visual documents and humans inspect them live.
what_it_does: Provides Blackboard files and tools for creating, reading, writing, patching, deleting, and validating structured text rendered as Unicode/ANSI visual scenes.
leverage_rationale: Structured source-authoritative canvas operations let agents manipulate a visual workspace precisely instead of guessing cell-level UI interactions.
leverage_evidence: Focused tools cover discovery, creation, reading, writing, patching, deletion, and validation.
Canvas immediately renders agent changes for human inspection.
Supports structured diagrams, tables, code, plots, and spatial layouts.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a broad coherent workspace and the demo is alive, but no video and limited visual proof cap confidence and completeness.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive and gallery_images=10.
Description states source is authoritative and canvas is live.
Frame sheets show dark/light canvas-like UI but text is too small for end-to-end verification.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real communication gap: agents produce text while humans often need visible structure, relationships, and spatial explanation.
impact_evidence: Use cases include teaching, research visualization, system mapping, interfaces, and presentations.
Shared human-agent visual medium is directly aligned with those needs.
creativity_rationale: A token-based visual medium native to both agent editing and human perception is a notably original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Unicode/ANSI canvas retains agent-readable structure while being visually inspectable.
Blackboard abstraction supports many visual document types.
Live shared result rather than plain chat output.
usability_note: Broad format support is powerful but may create complexity; live visual feedback is a strong aid.
red_flags: No video; breadth of claimed renderers and editing operations is not fully evidenced.
advance_reason: Original, useful medium with substantial WebMCP leverage; execution merits follow-up observation.

one_line: An agent-assisted stargazing planner that compares predictions with human observations.
what_it_does: Configures location/time/sky view, plans visible targets, produces printable guides and maps, and records observed-versus-predicted results.
leverage_rationale: Bundled configuration and observation workflow tools reduce setup friction and improve repeatability, but a general agent could achieve much of the same UI outcome with effort.
leverage_evidence: configure_sky_view sets location, time zone, local time, and view in one operation.
Agent plans targets while human observes.
Application records and compares predictions with observations.
execution_rationale: The live demo, repository, and extensive gallery indicate a thoughtfully scoped workflow, but there is no video and end-to-end agent execution is not directly shown.
execution_evidence: demo_alive=alive, public repo present, gallery_images=9.
Description lists sky configuration, printable guide, map, and observation comparison.
Frame sheets are UI contact sheets with limited readable detail.
impact_rationale: It serves beginners, families, travelers, and hobby astronomers by turning vague interest into a concrete observation plan and learning loop.
impact_evidence: Clear beginner-oriented decisions: visibility, timing, direction, targets, and recording.
Printable guide and what-if daylight comparison support practical use.
creativity_rationale: The prediction-versus-observation loop and agent-plans/human-observes division add a fresh angle to a stargazing guide.
creativity_evidence: Application records actual observations against fixed predictions.
What-if comparison reveals objects hidden by daylight.
usability_note: Concrete configuration and printable output should make the activity approachable for non-experts.
red_flags: No video; weather/sky-model accuracy and real observation flow are not demonstrated.
standouts: Strong educational loop from planning to field observation to comparison.
advance_reason: Credible and useful educational workflow with solid scope, pending direct observation.
